title: SAUR: Security Analysis & Threat Engine
category: AUR, SAUR, YARA, C++, C, CMAKE, SCANNER
excerpt: A deep dive into building a high-performance system auditor that leverages AVX2 vector instructions, YARA rule-sets, and live URLhaus threat feeds to scan files and memory for malicious payloads, credential leaks, and bad actors.
content:
If you guys remember the attacks on the AUR which have been a problem for a while—where malicious packages keep slipping through the cracks and targeting devs—that’s basically why I built **SAUR** all by myself. 

I needed a fast, no-nonsense system auditor that could actually tear through files and memory to sniff out bad actors, credential leaks, and malicious payloads before they ruin your day. Instead of relying on slow cloud scanners, I designed SAUR to use AVX2 vector instructions, YARA rulesets, and live URLhaus indicator feeds to do the heavy lifting locally.

### How it actually works under the hood

---

SAUR does a deep, recursive full-drive scan across your filesystem, intelligently dodging virtual directories (`/proc`, `/sys`, `/dev`) so it focuses strictly on real, physical files. Once it grabs a file, I built it to pipe it through four parallel analysis engines:

* **Hardware-Accelerated Signatures:** I wrote a custom NASM AVX2 SIMD kernel to push memory buffer scans for known malicious byte signatures at absolute hardware line speeds. 
* **Deterministic Pattern Matching (Google RE2):** Uses non-backtracking regular expressions to sniff out reverse shells, base64 obfuscation, privesc scripts, hardcoded AWS keys, private SSH keys, and Tor `.onion` addresses without blowing up on complex regex.
* **Live Threat Intelligence (Abuse.ch):** Pulls down the latest URLhaus threat feed live via LibCURL, cross-referencing contents against active malware drop sites straight in RAM.
* **YARA Rule Engine:** Compiles and runs heavy-duty offline YARA rulesets (like Neo23x0 signatures) against memory buffers using `libyara`.

### What you need to build it

---

You’ll need a modern Linux environment with C++20 support and a few standard dependencies. If you're on Arch, getting everything wired up is just one command:

```bash
sudo pacman -S --needed base-devel cmake nasm yara re2 curl git
```
(You'll also want GCC 11+ or Clang 13+ and CMake 3.16 or newer).

### Building and running it

---

Getting it compiled is standard boilerplate:

```bash

# 1. Clone the repo and jump in
git clone https://github.com/PicasoTheDeal/SAUR.git
cd SAUR

# 2. Spin up the build folder
mkdir build && cd build

# 3. Configure and compile
cmake ..
make

```

Because it's doing a full-drive audit and needs access to restricted paths, you’ll need root privileges to let it loose:

```bash
sudo ./compile/saur_daemon /
```

### A quick word on performance

---

Let’s be real, SAUR is buffering and analyzing every single regular file on your machine against thousands of regex patterns, heavy YARA rules, and live URLhaus indicators. If you point it at the root of an entire drive (`/`), it is going to hammer your CPU and disk I/O.

As the daemon output warns you: **It’s going to take time to scan whatever you've got on your PC**. Plan your audit windows accordingly and don't panic when your fans spin up.

It’s open-source under the MIT License—grab it, tweak it, and lock down your systems.
